clue.text: Hardly the role granted to a poor player

definitions.text: Hardly the role granted to a poor player

parts.words: Hardly the role granted to a poor player
parts.note: the most demanding leading part in Shakespeare is given only to a fine actor, never to a weak one

explanation.surface: A theatre director would not cast an inept actor in a starring part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poor player' echoes Macbeth's 'a poor player that struts and frets his hour upon the stage', steering you toward that play rather than its rival tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prince of Denmark is Shakespeare's longest and most coveted tragic role, reserved for leading actors.

clue.text: Totally inadequate instruction to avoid over-optimism

explanation.surface: Advice not to expect too much from a feeble effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as HOPE LESS, an order to expect less.
explanation.definitionFit: Utterly useless or incompetent is one sense; split into two words it advises lowering expectations.

clue.text: Minister a Conservative finds threatening

parts.note: MIN is an abbreviation for minister or ministry
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A government member discovers a party colleague is menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: A rare adjective for menacing, from the Latin for to threaten.

clue.text: Novel which upsets me to some degree

indicators.note: in a down clue upsets means the word me is turned upside down, reading bottom to top

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A book that troubles the reader up to a point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upsets' turns ME into EM; 'some degree' supplies MA. The novel is Jane Austen's 1815 story of a matchmaking heroine.
explanation.definitionFit: Jane Austen's 1815 work of fiction about a meddling matchmaker bears this title.

clue.text: Defector found in Filipino mountain country

parts.note: Mount Apo is the highest peak in the Philippines
a state is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A turncoat has been tracked down in the uplands of the Philippines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' is a link, not a container signal: the two pieces simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abandons a faith or cause is a renegade who has gone over to the other side.

clue.text: Crack down on negligent punctuation

parts.note: careless writing might end a sentence with a full stop dropped anywhere, read literally as inserting a stop

explanation.surface: Clamp down on sloppy commas and full stops.
explanation.walkthrough: A full stop is a punctuation mark, so the idiom for ending something is read as carelessly putting a period after a word.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something firmly is to halt or suppress it, an idiom for a clampdown.

clue.text: Reputed to be a descendant of Mohammed's daughter

explanation.surface: Believed to come from the Prophet's family line.
explanation.definitionFit: Something reputed is commonly stated or alleged; a sayyid (also spelt Said) is an honorific for those descended from Fatima, the Prophet's daughter.

clue.text: Bird sanctuary by railway beneath a Roman road

indicators.note: in a down clue beneath puts the railway piece lower in the column, after the road

parts.note: via is Latin for road, as in the Via Appia

explanation.surface: A refuge for birds next to the tracks, below an ancient highway.
explanation.definitionFit: A large enclosure where birds are kept and protected.

clue.text: Employ an egg-whisk with energy

indicators.note: to whisk is to beat and mix, so these letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Use a kitchen whisk vigorously to beat eggs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whisk' shuffles AN EGG into ENGAG, and E for energy finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To hire or take on staff is to give them work.

clue.text: Personal assistant meets a fellow returning from South American republic

indicators.note: returning means the words a fellow are read backwards, coming back the other way

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A secretary greets a man arriving home from Latin America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns A MAN into NAMA, which follows PA. The setter loosely places the isthmus republic in South America; it is usually counted as Central American.
explanation.definitionFit: The canal state at the narrow neck between the two Americas, once part of Colombia, is a republic.

clue.text: Dramatic protest by a disaffected work-force

explanation.surface: A theatrical walkout staged by unhappy employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dramatic is eye-catching and arresting; downing tools in protest is industrial action by walking out.

clue.text: A horseman drawn to Quatermain's inventor

parts.note: a horseman is a rider
drawn means looking haggard, gaunt and tired

explanation.surface: A cavalryman is attracted to the creator of a famous adventurer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawn to' looks like attraction, but drawn means gaunt. Allan Quatermain is the hunter-hero of the Victorian novelist's King Solomon's Mines.
explanation.definitionFit: H. Rider Haggard wrote King Solomon's Mines and created the adventurer Allan Quatermain.

clue.text: Many belonged to Abraham's nephew

explanation.surface: Plenty of property was owned by a Biblical patriarch's relative.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as LOT'S, the possessive of Lot, nephew of Abraham in the Book of Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: A large number is plenty; Lot was Abraham's nephew in Genesis, so his possessions were his by the possessive form.

clue.text: Foremost avenue of trees

parts.note: firs are coniferous trees, giving the singular form of the species name
ST is the standard abbreviation for street, a road or avenue

explanation.surface: The finest of tree-lined boulevards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link here; the conifer comes before the road abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at the very front or top of a ranking means leading all the others.

clue.text: Penny-dreadful featuring transvestite habits

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for an old British penny, from the Latin denarius
a rag is a dreadful, low-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A cheap Victorian thriller about men dressing as women.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penny-dreadful' poses as one compound (a lurid cheap serial) but splits into D, the pre-decimal penny, and RAG, a trashy paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothing of the opposite sex, especially women's dress worn by men, is the costume of a drag queen.

clue.text: Courteous rendition of 101+6+50

parts.note: CI is 101 in Roman numerals
VI is 6 in Roman numerals
L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A polite version of a sum of numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendition' asks for the numbers rendered as Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: Polite and well-mannered behaviour is civil.

clue.text: Has New York the capacity to be circumspect?

parts.note: to have the capacity to do something is to be able, so can

explanation.surface: Does the Big Apple have it in it to be cautious?
explanation.definitionFit: Shrewd and careful, especially with money, is a Scots word for prudent.

clue.text: A female priest in the armed forces

definitions.text: A female priest in the armed forces

parts.words: A female priest in the armed forces
parts.note: a woman who leads church worship could be described as a woman of the service, punning on the military services

explanation.surface: A woman chaplain serving with the military.
explanation.walkthrough: A priest conducts a church service, so the clue toys with reading a member of the forces as a woman who takes services.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman enlisted in the army, navy or air force is a member of one of the services.

clue.text: Uncompromising support for Diana in the area

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits below, so the uncompromising word goes underneath the name

parts.note: Di is the short form of the name Diana
strict means rigid and uncompromising

explanation.surface: Unyielding backing for a princess in the region.
explanation.definitionFit: A region or administrative division of a country or town.

clue.text: Like fish jelly

parts.note: a seaweed-based setting agent that works much as gelatin made from fish does

explanation.surface: Something resembling a fishy aspic.
explanation.walkthrough: The jelly comes from seaweed rather than fish, but it serves the same purpose as isinglass, a gelatin from fish bladders.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous substance from red seaweed, used as a vegetarian setting agent and culture medium.

clue.text: Elevated status never achieved by lying low

definitions.text: Elevated status never achieved by lying low

parts.words: Elevated status never achieved by lying low
parts.note: prestige is set against its literal opposite: one cannot be upright and tall while lying flat on the ground

explanation.surface: You won't get to the top by keeping your head down.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminent rank or good repute in society is a lofty position.

clue.text: Cockchafer leaves visible sign of damage on Jack

indicators.note: in a down clue on places the mark above, so it comes first in the column

parts.note: a scar is the mark left by an injury
a jack tar is a sailor, and AB (able seaman) is a sailor

explanation.surface: A beetle leaves a mark on a man called Jack.
explanation.definitionFit: The cockchafer is a member of the dung-beetle family, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Dentures on which food gets stuck

explanation.surface: False teeth that trap bits of dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: False teeth are fixed to a dental plate; dishes are what meals are served on.

clue.text: Some leg of veal

explanation.surface: A cut from the leg of a young cow.
explanation.definitionFit: The back of the lower leg is one part of it; veal is the meat of a young bovine, sold under that animal's name as in calf's liver.

clue.text: Ismaili leader elected once more

parts.note: the Aga Khan is the hereditary imam of the Ismaili Muslims, and Aga is a title of command
a candidate who is elected is in office

explanation.surface: A Muslim spiritual head wins a further term of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something a second time means repeating it anew.

clue.text: Cause trouble in gaol

explanation.surface: Make a fuss while locked up in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: GAOL is the British spelling of jail; STIR is old slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To agitate or incite unrest is to stir things up; slang for prison is the same word.

clue.text: A common error, whichever way one views it

indicators.note: the word reads the same forwards and backwards, so it looks identical from either direction

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A frequent blunder, however you look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British slang for a silly mistake or blunder.

clue.text: Ground mace is the crowning glory

indicators.note: ground, as in milled or crushed, signals the letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Freshly milled spice is the finest touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ground' suggests the spice crushed; it shuffles MACE.
explanation.definitionFit: The peak or highest point of achievement.

clue.text: Reasonable allowance needing a pound extra

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance of food or supplies
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from the Latin libra

explanation.surface: A fair weekly sum that could do with an extra quid.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensible and logical, based on reason rather than emotion.

clue.text: Yearning to be a successor to the Mings

parts.note: the Ch'ing (Qing) dynasty followed the Ming dynasty as rulers of China

explanation.surface: Longing to follow in the footsteps of Chinese emperors.
explanation.walkthrough: CHING is the older spelling of the Qing dynasty, which took over China from the Ming in 1644.
explanation.definitionFit: Longing painfully for something is a hurting desire.

clue.text: An energetic group out to make mischief

parts.note: busy means active and energetic
a body is an organised group, as in a governing body

explanation.surface: A lively gang of troublemakers is on the loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A meddler who interferes in other people's affairs stirs up trouble.

clue.text: Right man to lead the England selectors

definitions.text: man to lead the England selectors

explanation.surface: The correct person to head the national cricket selection panel.
explanation.walkthrough: Ted Dexter, a former England cricket captain, became chairman of the England selectors in 1989, around when this puzzle appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: In heraldry the right-hand side of a shield is the dexter side; Ted Dexter chaired England's cricket selection panel from 1989.
